Q5651.reason: The 'as is' clause disclaims quality/condition warranties but not the express warranty/description (1964 model) that was part of the basis of the bargain, so the seller is likely liable.

Q5672.reason: If the shooter's acquittal rested on self-defense, the killing was justified, so there is no unlawful homicide for the accessory to be guilty of, whereas insanity or diminished capacity are personal excuses that don't free the instigator.

Q8537.reason: Separating the concept from its justification keeps the definition of punishment value-neutral so that justification can be argued separately.
